title: Cerebral white matter hyperintensities volume predicted effector genes (Sargurupremraj M et al. 2020)
bodyHtml:
This table lists genes implicated in cerebral white matter hyperinstensities (WMH) volume, which is associated with cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), from the study:

Cerebral small vessel disease genomics and its implications across the lifespan
Sargurupremraj M, Suzuki H, Jian X, Sarnowski C, Evans TE, Bis JC, et al. 
Nat Commun. 2020 Dec 8;11(1):6285. doi: 10.1038/s41467-020-19111-2.
PMID: 33293549

In this study, the authors investigate white matter hyperintensities (WMH), a common brain-imaging feature associated with cerebral small vessel disease (SVD). While hypertension is a well-known risk factor for WMH, the authors identify 27 genome-wide loci linked to WMH-volume in a cohort of 50,970 older individuals, while also considering the influence of hypertension. The aggregation of WMH risk variants is found to impact white matter integrity in the brains of young, healthy adults, shedding light on the lifelong consequences of genetic risk for SVD.

Moreover, Mendelian randomization analysis indicates a causal relationship between increasing WMH-volume and conditions such as stroke and Alzheimer-type dementia. It also suggests that higher blood pressure is associated with larger WMH-volume, even in individuals without clinical hypertension. Transcriptome-wide colocalization analyses reveal connections between WMH-volume and the expression of 39 genes, with four of them encoding known drug targets. This research provides insights into biological pathways underlying SVD, independent of blood pressure, and suggests the potential for genetic stratification of high-risk individuals and the prioritization of drug targets for prevention trials.
